locators: Process paragraph beginning with Nabarangpur and Balasore, between image labels IN548.2 and IN548.5

claims: Its process account describes hand-shaping fine clay, drying, firing in a kiln, coating with lac and adding contrasting threadlike decorative elements.
The entry describes paired male/female dolls and their marriage-related significance; retain attribution if used.
Its collection includes a Ganesha figure as well as four jaukandhei figures, purchased in2017at the Crafts Council in New Delhi.
limits: Acquisition date is not object manufacture date. The final paragraph does not identify each object's maker; do not attribute these specific objects to Kesudas merely because he is mentioned nearby.
Do not repeat very-few-makers claims, exclusivity to one district, current exhibition status, or exact drying times as universal practice.
The entry first calls the craft unique to Balasore then names Nabarangpur too. Avoid an exclusivity claim and do not flatten regional practices.
Vegetable/natural dye wording is not evidence that every present object is chemical-free, safe for children or environmentally benign.

sources.title: The Jaukandhei lac doll-making tradition of Odisha sees a revival
sources.author: Ashis Senapati
sources.access: Full original-publisher AMP article inspected; regular route found in publisher indexed results. These are one source, not independent corroboration.
locators: Opening reporting and Kanakalata Das testimony, lines27–31
claims: Senapati reports Kanakalata Das and other women applying coloured lac to figurines; describes clay shaping, firing and lacquer finish in Balasore.
Kanakalata Das tells him that Binapani SHG was formed with15women in2005; the report locates her group in Koshamba Nagar on Balasore's outskirts.
Named craftspeople discuss festivals, making and selling. Use dated, attributed testimony rather than general economic conclusions.
Kesu Das describes ceremonial doll weddings and offerings during Sabitri Brata; usable sparingly as his account, not a uniform rule for all households.
limits: Do not reproduce the reporter's staged opening as the project's own witnessed scene.
Keep2005formation testimony and2022reporting dates separate. The group size is not a verified2026membership figure.
Do not conflate Binapani SHG with Mission Shakti's Bampada Producer Group.

Exclude current prices/income/maker totals, timeless origin language, revival percentage, decline causation and plastic-versus-lac environmental claims. These would need narrower verification and add little to the chosen essay.

recommended_shape: A compact material-and-maker essay: form and surface, named makers, one historical collective-work example, and specific collected objects. Avoid the discovery site's structure, encyclopedic origin stories or repeated research narration. The paired figures or Ganesha can add specificity without adding another source family. Ganjapa and existing material-arts/clay-toy articles provide reading connections, not substitute evidence.
